import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()

    # Sort by user_id, then event_ts, then event_id
    events = events.sort_values(by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Extract date (calendar date in server local time)
    events["event_date"] = events["event_ts"].dt.date

    # Previous row values (shifted)
    prev_user = events["user_id"].shift(1)
    prev_ts = events["event_ts"].shift(1)
    prev_date = events["event_date"].shift(1)

    # Determine if this event starts a new session
    different_user = events["user_id"] != prev_user
    different_date = events["event_date"] != prev_date

    # gap in minutes; for first row of each series, prev_ts is NaT -> gap comparison False,
    # but different_user already True for first row of each user, so it's fine.
    gap_minutes = (events["event_ts"] - prev_ts).dt.total_seconds() / 60.0
    gap_exceeded = gap_minutes > 45

    new_session = different_user | different_date | gap_exceeded

    # Session number per user via cumulative sum of new_session flags
    events["session_num"] = new_session.groupby(events["user_id"]).cumsum().astype("int64")

    # Group by user_id and session_num to build sessions
    user_sessions = events.groupby(["user_id", "session_num"], as_index=False).agg(
        session_date=("event_date", "first"),
        session_start=("event_ts", "min"),
        session_end=("event_ts", "max"),
        event_count=("event_id", "count"),
    )

    # Ensure correct types
    user_sessions["user_id"] = user_sessions["user_id"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_num"] = user_sessions["session_num"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_date"] = user_sessions["session_date"].astype("object")  # Keep as date object
    user_sessions["session_start"] = user_sessions["session_start"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    user_sessions["session_end"] = user_sessions["session_end"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    user_sessions["event_count"] = user_sessions["event_count"].astype("int64")

    # Sort output by user_id and session_num
    user_sessions = user_sessions.sort_values(by=["user_id", "session_num"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    return {"user_sessions": user_sessions}
